project.name: chatbot
project.description: A full-stack agentic RAG chatbot: React 19 + Vite frontend, FastAPI backend running a LangGraph state-machine RAG pipeline (hybrid pgvector + Postgres FTS retrieval with RRF fusion, OpenRouter reranking/embeddings/chat), PostgreSQL, Celery + Redis background jobs, JWT auth, and a standalone PaddleOCR microservice.

nodes.name: env.py
nodes.summary: Alembic migration environment that wires the app's SQLAlchemy metadata and database URL into online/offline migration runners.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard Alembic env.py boilerplate reusing the app's Settings and Base.metadata as the migration target.

nodes.name: database.py
nodes.summary: Sets up the SQLAlchemy engine, SessionLocal factory, and declarative Base, and exposes the get_db request-scoped session dependency.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application entry point that mounts the auth, chat, conversations, and documents routers, request-logging middleware, and a health endpoint.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy ORM models for the RAG chatbot: documents, parent/child chunks, users, conversations, and messages.
nodes.languageNotes: Parent/child chunk split (DocumentParentChunk vs DocumentChunk) mirrors the retrieval strategy where children are retrieved but parents are returned to the LLM.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the FastAPI routers package.

nodes.name: auth.py
nodes.summary: Authentication router exposing a login endpoint that verifies credentials and mints a JWT, plus a /me endpoint returning the current user.

nodes.name: chat.py
nodes.summary: Chat router that validates the target document, persists conversation/message rows, and streams the agentic RAG answer as server-sent events.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a fresh SessionLocal inside the SSE generator so the streaming DB work is decoupled from the request-scoped session.

nodes.name: conversations.py
nodes.summary: Conversations router providing per-user CRUD: list, fetch with messages, delete a single conversation, and clear all conversations.

nodes.name: documents.py
nodes.summary: Documents router that lists ingested documents, handles validated file uploads dispatched to Celery ingestion, and streams ingestion status over SSE.

nodes.name: schemas.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic request/response schemas for documents, chat, auth tokens, users, conversations, and messages used across the API layer.

nodes.name: security.py
nodes.summary: Security utilities: passlib password hashing/verification, JWT access-token creation, and the get_current_user OAuth2 dependency used to guard routes.

nodes.name: create_user.py
nodes.summary: CLI script that creates or updates a user account with a hashed password directly against the database.

nodes.name: reingest_all.py
nodes.summary: Maintenance CLI that re-runs the parse/chunk/embed/store ingestion pipeline for one or all documents after a chunk-schema change.

nodes.name: conftest.py
nodes.summary: Pytest fixtures that build tables, provide a transaction-rolled-back DB session, and a TestClient with the get_db dependency overridden.

nodes.name: test_auth.py
nodes.summary: Tests covering login success/failure, the /me endpoint, and that protected chat and document routes require a valid token.

nodes.name: Document
nodes.summary: ORM model for an uploaded document, tracking file name, storage path, ingestion status, and metadata.

nodes.name: DocumentParentChunk
nodes.summary: ORM model for large parent chunks (~1500 tokens) that are returned to the LLM after their child chunks are retrieved.

nodes.name: DocumentChunk
nodes.summary: ORM model for retrievable child chunks (~300 tokens) holding the embedding vector, FTS text, and link back to a parent chunk.

nodes.name: User
nodes.summary: ORM model for an authenticated user with username, hashed password, and active flag.

nodes.name: Conversation
nodes.summary: ORM model for a chat conversation owned by a user, with title and created/updated timestamps.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: ORM model for a single chat message with role, content, citations, and optional document association.

nodes.name: get_db
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency that yields a request-scoped SQLAlchemy session and rolls back / closes it on teardown.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: Login handler that looks up the user, verifies the password, and returns a JWT access token or a 401 on failure.

nodes.name: chat_stream
nodes.summary: Validates the document, ensures/creates the conversation, persists the user and assistant messages, and streams the agentic RAG answer plus citations as SSE.

nodes.name: list_conversations
nodes.summary: Returns the current user's conversations ordered by most recently updated.

nodes.name: get_conversation
nodes.summary: Fetches a single conversation owned by the user along with its ordered messages, returning 404 if not found.

nodes.name: delete_conversation
nodes.summary: Deletes a single user-owned conversation, returning 404 if it does not exist.

nodes.name: clear_conversations
nodes.summary: Deletes all conversations belonging to the current user.

nodes.name: upload_document
nodes.summary: Validates file type and size, persists the upload to disk and a pending Document row, then dispatches the ingestion task to Celery.

nodes.name: stream_status
nodes.summary: Polls a document's ingestion status in a fresh session and streams status updates to the client as server-sent events.

nodes.name: create_access_token
nodes.summary: Builds a signed JWT access token for a subject with a configurable expiry.

nodes.name: get_current_user
nodes.summary: OAuth2 dependency that decodes the JWT, loads the matching user, and raises 401 on invalid or missing credentials.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI arguments and creates or updates a user record with a bcrypt-hashed password.

nodes.name: reingest_one
nodes.summary: Re-ingests a single document by clearing its chunks and re-running parse, chunk, embed, and store, updating status and handling failures.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that selects target documents (single id or by status) and reingests each in turn.

nodes.name: client.js
nodes.summary: Central API client wrapper that stores the JWT in localStorage, injects the Authorization header on every request via apiFetch, and dispatches an auth:unauthorized window event on 401 responses so AuthContext can log the user out and redirect to /login.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a custom window event (auth:unauthorized) as a decoupled signal so a low-level fetch wrapper can trigger app-level logout without importing React context directly.

nodes.name: getToken
nodes.summary: Reads the persisted JWT from localStorage under the TOKEN_KEY key.

nodes.name: setToken
nodes.summary: Persists or clears the JWT in localStorage depending on whether a truthy token is provided.

nodes.name: authHeaders
nodes.summary: Builds a headers object merging any extra headers with a Bearer Authorization header when a token is present.

nodes.name: apiFetch
nodes.summary: Wraps the native fetch to auto-attach auth headers and, on a 401 response, clears the token and broadcasts an auth:unauthorized event for global logout handling.

nodes.name: ChatMessage.jsx
nodes.summary: Renders a single chat message bubble (user or assistant) with lightweight markdown formatting (bold text, numbered label lists), an expandable citations panel, and message action buttons (feedback, copy, regenerate).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML for inline bold-text rendering; the input is regex-transformed message content rather than raw user HTML, but it is a spot worth revisiting if message content is ever untrusted.

nodes.name: renderContent
nodes.summary: Parses raw assistant message text into React elements, converting **bold** markup and numbered '1. **Label:** body' lines into a definition-style ordered list.

nodes.name: ChatMessage
nodes.summary: Default-exported component that renders a user or assistant chat bubble, showing a ThinkingIndicator while streaming, an expandable citations list, and per-message action buttons.

nodes.name: ChatThread.jsx
nodes.summary: Scrollable message list component that renders the conversation's messages as ChatMessage bubbles and auto-scrolls to the newest message.

nodes.name: ChatThread
nodes.summary: Maps the messages array to ChatMessage components and keeps the view pinned to the bottom via a ref-based auto-scroll effect.

nodes.name: Composer.jsx
nodes.summary: Message input composer with an auto-resizing textarea, Enter-to-send keyboard handling, and a file-attachment control that surfaces a selected-file chip with upload progress state.

nodes.name: Composer
nodes.summary: Manages composer text and selected-file state, wiring submit-on-Enter, textarea auto-grow, and file-picker upload handoff via onSend/onFileSelect callbacks.

nodes.name: DocumentSelector.jsx
nodes.summary: Dropdown selector that fetches the list of ingested documents from the backend and lets the user choose which document to chat with, refreshing on window focus.

nodes.name: DocumentSelector
nodes.summary: Loads documents via apiFetch on mount and window focus, then renders them as a select bound to the parent's selected document id.

nodes.name: ThinkingIndicator.jsx
nodes.summary: Whimsical animated status indicator shown while the assistant is generating a response, rotating through status words and surfacing a 'taking longer than expected' hint after 12 seconds.

nodes.name: ThinkingIndicator
nodes.summary: Cycles through a list of status words on an interval and flags a long-wait state after a timeout, rendering an accessible status region.

nodes.name: UpgradeTab.jsx
nodes.summary: Trivial presentational 'Upgrade to Pro' call-to-action banner with no internal state or logic.

nodes.name: UpgradeTab
nodes.summary: Renders a static clickable upgrade-to-Pro badge.

nodes.name: UploadToast.jsx
nodes.summary: Toast notification that reports document ingestion success or failure, auto-dismissing after 5 seconds once the upload reaches a terminal state.

nodes.name: UploadToast
nodes.summary: Renders a success/failure toast for document ingestion status and auto-dismisses via a timeout effect tied to the status prop.

nodes.name: useChat.js
nodes.summary: Custom hook implementing the chat conversation state machine: dispatches user/assistant messages through a reducer and streams assistant responses from the backend's SSE-style /api/chat/stream endpoint, parsing token/citations/done/error events.
nodes.languageNotes: Manually parses a fetch() streaming response body (reader.read + TextDecoder) as newline-delimited 'data: {...}' SSE events rather than using EventSource, since it needs to POST a body.

nodes.name: reducer
nodes.summary: Reducer handling chat state transitions: adding user/assistant messages, appending streamed tokens, setting citations, marking streaming end/error, and resetting or loading a persisted conversation.

nodes.name: useChat
nodes.summary: Hook exposing handleSend/loadMessages/reset; handleSend posts to /api/chat/stream and incrementally parses the streamed response to dispatch token, citation, and completion events into the reducer.

nodes.name: useConversations.js
nodes.summary: Custom hook managing the sidebar conversation list — loading, deleting, and clearing conversations via the conversation repository.

nodes.name: useConversations
nodes.summary: Fetches and caches the conversation list on mount, exposing refresh/remove/clearAll operations backed by conversationRepository.

nodes.name: useUpload.js
nodes.summary: Custom hook that uploads a file to the backend and tracks ingestion progress via a Server-Sent Events connection to the document status endpoint.

nodes.name: useUpload
nodes.summary: Uploads a file via multipart form data, then opens an EventSource against /api/documents/{id}/status to track processing until done/failed, exposing state, uploadFile, and reset.

nodes.name: ChatPage.jsx
nodes.summary: Top-level chat page that wires together the sidebar, document selector, chat thread, composer, and upload toast, orchestrating the useChat/useConversations/useUpload hooks into a cohesive chat experience.

nodes.name: ChatPage
nodes.summary: Composes the chat UI, manages selected-document/active-conversation/toast state, and defines callbacks for sending messages, switching or deleting conversations, and handling uploads.

nodes.name: conversationRepository.js
nodes.summary: Repository-pattern data-access module for chat-history conversations, wrapping apiFetch calls to list, fetch, delete, and clear conversations.

nodes.name: listConversations
nodes.summary: Fetches the list of conversations (id, title, timestamps) from /api/conversations.

nodes.name: getConversation
nodes.summary: Fetches a single conversation with its full message history by id.

nodes.name: deleteConversation
nodes.summary: Deletes a single conversation by id.

nodes.name: clearConversations
nodes.summary: Deletes all conversations for the current user.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Centralized application settings loaded from the environment via a pydantic Settings class, covering database, Redis, OpenRouter/OpenAI credentials, JWT auth, retrieval and rerank tuning, and OCR service configuration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a pydantic settings class with typed fields for environment-driven configuration.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: Typed settings object exposing all runtime configuration: database and Redis URLs, LLM/embedding/rerank model names and credentials, JWT auth parameters, upload limits, retrieval tuning knobs, and OCR options.

nodes.name: ingestion.py
nodes.summary: Document ingestion pipeline that parses PDFs, DOCX, and images (with OCR fallback), splits text into parent (~1500 token) and child (~300 token) chunks, embeds children via OpenRouter, and persists parent/child chunks to the database.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the parent-child chunking strategy central to the RAG retrieval design.

nodes.name: PageContent
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing one parsed page's text along with its page number, source (native or OCR), and OCR confidence.

nodes.name: ParsedDocument
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding all parsed pages plus document metadata, with a helper that concatenates page text.

nodes.name: ParentChunk
nodes.summary: Dataclass for a large parent chunk (~1500 tokens) spanning a page range, returned to the LLM as retrieval context.

nodes.name: ChildChunk
nodes.summary: Dataclass for a small child chunk (~300 tokens) that gets embedded and retrieved, carrying its page number and OCR confidence.

nodes.name: _ocr_page_image
nodes.summary: Runs OCR on a single page image via the OCR client, returning extracted text and confidence and logging a warning on failure.

nodes.name: _parse_pdf
nodes.summary: Parses a PDF page-by-page with PyMuPDF, using native text when present and falling back to OCR on the rendered page image for scanned pages.

nodes.name: parse_document
nodes.summary: Dispatches a file to the appropriate parser (PDF, DOCX, or image) by extension and returns a ParsedDocument with page content and metadata.

nodes.name: chunk_text
nodes.summary: Splits text into parent chunks and then each parent into child chunks using tiktoken-based recursive splitters, returning parents with their children.

nodes.name: chunk_document
nodes.summary: Chunks a parsed document into parent and child chunks, propagating page numbers and source metadata and skipping blank pages.

nodes.name: embed_text
nodes.summary: Embeds a single text string into a 1536-dim vector via the OpenRouter-compatible embeddings API.

nodes.name: embed_chunks
nodes.summary: Batch-embeds child chunk texts into vectors via the embeddings API, logging progress across batches.

nodes.name: store_chunks
nodes.summary: Persists parent chunks and their embedded child chunks to the database, linking children to their parents and committing in bulk.

nodes.name: ocr_client.py
nodes.summary: HTTP client that sends image bytes to the PaddleOCR microservice and returns joined text with averaged confidence, raising OCRError on transport failures.

nodes.name: ocr_image
nodes.summary: POSTs image bytes to the OCR microservice, joins returned line texts, averages line confidences, and raises OCRError on HTTP failure.

nodes.name: graph.py
nodes.summary: Assembles and runs the LangGraph agentic RAG state machine, wiring the six nodes together with conditional retry routing and streaming answer tokens and citations to callers.
nodes.languageNotes: LangGraph StateGraph with conditional edges and async streaming via astream_events.

nodes.name: build_graph
nodes.summary: Constructs the LangGraph StateGraph, registering the six RAG nodes and wiring linear edges plus the conditional retry edge out of grading.

nodes.name: _build_citations
nodes.summary: Deduplicates parent chunks into an ordered list of citations with page number and source for the final answer.

nodes.name: agentic_rag_stream
nodes.summary: Async generator that runs the compiled RAG graph, streaming answer tokens as they generate and emitting a final citations and warnings payload.

nodes.name: nodes.py
nodes.summary: Implements the individual LangGraph nodes of the agentic RAG pipeline: query rewrite, retrieve-and-rerank, chunk grading, retry rewrite, answer generation, and faithfulness check.

nodes.name: rewrite_query
nodes.summary: First graph node: rewrites the user question into a retrieval-optimized query and classifies intent using a structured-output LLM call.

nodes.name: retrieve_and_rerank
nodes.summary: Graph node that runs hybrid retrieval and reranking for the current query, writing retrieved children, parents, and scores into the state.

nodes.name: grade_chunks
nodes.summary: Graph node that judges whether retrieved chunks are useful, using a fast rerank-score-floor path or an LLM grader depending on configuration.

nodes.name: rewrite_and_retry
nodes.summary: Graph node that generates a new query variation for another retrieval attempt when grading found the chunks insufficient.

nodes.name: generate_answer
nodes.summary: Graph node that formats parent chunks into context and prompts the LLM to generate the grounded answer.

nodes.name: faithfulness_check
nodes.summary: Final graph node that asks the LLM whether the answer is grounded in the context and appends a warning if it is not.

nodes.name: prompts.py
nodes.summary: Prompt template string constants used by the RAG nodes for grading chunk relevance, rewriting queries on retry, and checking answer faithfulness.

nodes.name: reranker.py
nodes.summary: Cross-encoder reranking client that scores retrieved chunks against the query via OpenRouter's /v1/rerank endpoint, sorting by score and falling back to input order on API errors.

nodes.name: rerank
nodes.summary: Reranks candidate chunks against the query via OpenRouter's /v1/rerank cross-encoder, returning the top-N by score and falling back to input order on error.

nodes.name: retrieval.py
nodes.summary: Hybrid retrieval layer that runs pgvector similarity and Postgres FTS searches, fuses them with reciprocal rank fusion, reranks, applies metadata boosts, and returns parent chunks for the LLM.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines pgvector cosine-distance queries with Postgres full-text search fused via RRF.

nodes.name: hybrid_search
nodes.summary: Runs pgvector cosine-distance vector search and Postgres full-text search over a document's chunks, with optional page-range filtering.

nodes.name: rrf_fuse
nodes.summary: Fuses the vector and FTS ranked lists into a single ordering using reciprocal rank fusion.

nodes.name: fetch_parents
nodes.summary: Maps reranked child chunks to their parent chunks, deduplicating while preserving first-appearance order.

nodes.name: apply_metadata_boost
nodes.summary: Adjusts rerank scores using chunk metadata, promoting native-text chunks and penalizing low-confidence OCR chunks, then re-sorts.

nodes.name: retrieve
nodes.summary: Top-level retrieval orchestration: hybrid search, RRF fusion, rerank, metadata boost, and parent fetch, returning parent chunks for answer generation.

nodes.name: state.py
nodes.summary: Defines the AgentState TypedDict carrying data through the RAG graph and a factory that builds the initial state for a question.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: TypedDict describing the full state threaded through the RAG graph, including query, retrieved chunks, rerank scores, answer, citations, and warnings.

nodes.name: initial_state
nodes.summary: Builds the initial AgentState for a document and question with empty retrieval and answer fields and zeroed retry counters.

nodes.name: celery_app.py
nodes.summary: Configures the Celery application (broker and backend from settings) and registers worker signal handlers for rotating-file logging and startup task logging.

nodes.name: tasks.py
nodes.summary: Celery task that runs the full document ingestion pipeline (parse, chunk, embed, store) for an uploaded document, updating its status to done or failed with retry on error.

nodes.name: ingest_document
nodes.summary: Celery task orchestrating the ingestion pipeline for one document: parse, chunk, embed, and store, marking status done on success or failed with retry on error.

nodes.name: test_rag_graph.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the RAG graph's route_after_grade conditional routing, covering the generate, retry-under-budget, and give-up-when-exhausted branches.

nodes.name: App.jsx
nodes.summary: Root React component that wraps the tree in AuthProvider and defines the client-side route table (home, login, and the protected chat page) via react-router-dom.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Declares the app's routes (/, /login, /chat) inside AuthProvider and BrowserRouter, gating /chat behind ProtectedRoute so only authenticated users reach ChatPage.

nodes.name: AuthContext.jsx
nodes.summary: Defines the AuthContext and AuthProvider component that own token/user/loading state, validate a persisted token on mount, react to a global unauthorized event, and expose login/logout plus the useAuth hook to the rest of the app.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses React context + a custom useAuth hook (the standard provider/consumer pattern) and a window CustomEvent ('auth:unauthorized') as a lightweight cross-component signal so the API client can force a logout without a direct dependency on this file.

nodes.name: AuthProvider
nodes.summary: Provider component holding token/user/loading state; on mount it revalidates a stored token via getMe, clears state on 'auth:unauthorized' events, and exposes memoized login/logout callbacks through context.

nodes.name: useAuth
nodes.summary: Hook that reads AuthContext and throws if called outside an AuthProvider, giving consumers access to token, user, loading, isAuthenticated, login, and logout.

nodes.name: ProtectedRoute.jsx
nodes.summary: Route guard component that redirects unauthenticated visitors to /login (preserving the intended destination in router state) and renders children once auth state is confirmed.

nodes.name: ProtectedRoute
nodes.summary: Reads isAuthenticated/loading from useAuth; renders nothing while a stored token is being validated, redirects to /login with the current location saved for post-login return, or renders the protected children.

nodes.name: Sidebar.jsx
nodes.summary: Sidebar UI listing conversations with new-chat/search actions, hover-revealed delete buttons, and a footer showing the logged-in user's initials plus a logout button, sourcing auth state from useAuth.

nodes.name: ChatIcon
nodes.summary: Small presentational SVG chat-bubble icon whose stroke color changes when the parent conversation item is active.

nodes.name: Sidebar
nodes.summary: Renders the sidebar layout (logo, new-chat/search actions, conversation list with hover-reveal delete, and footer with settings/logout/user avatar), driven by conversations/activeId/onSelect/onNewChat/onDelete/onClearAll props and the authenticated user from useAuth.

nodes.name: main.jsx
nodes.summary: Vite/React entry point that mounts the root App component inside StrictMode onto the #root DOM element and loads the global stylesheet.

nodes.name: HomePage.jsx
nodes.summary: Landing/marketing page presenting the 'CHAT A.I+' brand with call-to-action buttons that navigate the user into the /chat route.

nodes.name: HomePage
nodes.summary: Renders the home hero section with tagline and two CTA buttons, both of which navigate to /chat via useNavigate.

nodes.name: LoginPage.jsx
nodes.summary: Login form page that collects username/password, calls the auth context's login action, and redirects to the originally requested route (or /chat) on success while surfacing errors inline.

nodes.name: LoginPage
nodes.summary: Renders the sign-in form; on submit it calls useAuth().login, then navigates to the redirect target saved in router location state (defaulting to /chat), showing an inline error and disabling the submit button while pending.

nodes.name: authRepository.js
nodes.summary: Repository-pattern data-access module for authentication endpoints; wraps fetch calls to /api/auth/login and /api/auth/me so UI components never call fetch directly.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the repository-abstraction convention called out in the project's CLAUDE.md: data-fetching is isolated here rather than inlined in components/hooks.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: POSTs { username, password } to /api/auth/login and returns the parsed { access_token, token_type } response, throwing an Error (annotated with .status) using the server's detail message on failure.

nodes.name: getMe
nodes.summary: Fetches the current authenticated user from /api/auth/me using a bearer token, throwing if the request is not authenticated.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the agentic RAG service that re-exports the public entry point (agentic_rag_stream) from graph.py so callers can import from app.services.rag directly.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package __init__ used purely as a re-export surface for the LangGraph RAG state machine.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: Computes RAG evaluation metrics for the golden-set harness: RAGAS scores (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall) via an OpenRouter LLM judge plus lightweight custom checks and per-run aggregation.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds a ChatOpenAI judge and OpenAIEmbeddings pointed at OpenRouter, then hands a HuggingFace Dataset to ragas.evaluate.

nodes.name: run_eval.py
nodes.summary: CLI eval harness that runs the golden question set through the agentic RAG stream, scores answers with the metrics module, and saves/compares timestamped JSON result snapshots (python -m evals.run_eval --name / --compare).
nodes.languageNotes: Async orchestration driven by asyncio.run; stamps runs with the current git SHA for reproducible baselines.

nodes.name: test_eval_golden.py
nodes.summary: Pytest test (marked eval) that runs the golden set end-to-end and asserts the aggregated summary metrics meet minimum quality thresholds.
nodes.languageNotes: Excluded from default pytest runs via the @pytest.mark.eval marker (addopts = -m 'not eval').

nodes.name: run_ragas_metrics
nodes.summary: Assembles questions/answers/contexts/ground-truths into a Dataset and runs ragas.evaluate with an LLM judge and embeddings, returning per-question faithfulness, answer relevancy, and context precision/recall lists.

nodes.name: expected_substring_match
nodes.summary: Case-insensitive check for whether the model's answer contains an expected substring, used as a deterministic correctness signal.

nodes.name: answered
nodes.summary: Boolean check that the model produced a non-empty, substantive answer for a question.

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Aggregates per-question metric dictionaries into run-level averages and pass counts for the eval summary block.

nodes.name: _resolve_document_id
nodes.summary: Looks up an ingested Document by file name (status='done') and returns its id, raising if the document has not been ingested.

nodes.name: _run_one
nodes.summary: Streams a single question through agentic_rag_stream for a document, collecting the streamed tokens into a final answer string.

nodes.name: run_eval
nodes.summary: Core async harness that iterates the golden set, runs each question through the RAG stream, scores answers with RAGAS and custom checks, and assembles a full result payload with metadata and summary.

nodes.name: _compare
nodes.summary: Loads two saved eval runs by name and prints a side-by-side comparison of their summary metrics for regression checking.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses --name/--compare arguments and either runs a new eval (saving results) or compares two existing runs.

nodes.name: test_golden_set_runs_and_summary_meets_thresholds
nodes.summary: Eval-marked pytest that runs the golden set via run_eval and asserts the summary metrics clear minimum quality thresholds.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Excludes node_modules, dist, git metadata, IDE files, and markdown/docs from the Docker build context so root-context image builds stay fast and don't leak source-control or documentation artifacts.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full application stack — nginx-served React frontend, FastAPI backend, Celery worker, PaddleOCR microservice, Redis, and a pgvector-enabled Postgres database — wiring build contexts, healthchecks, volumes, and startup ordering via depends_on conditions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses depends_on with service_healthy/service_started conditions to sequence startup across six interdependent containers rather than relying on fixed sleep delays.

nodes.name: frontend
nodes.summary: Builds and runs the React/Vite frontend from the root Dockerfile, mapping host port 3000 to nginx's port 80, and waits for the backend to report healthy before starting.

nodes.name: backend
nodes.summary: Builds and runs the FastAPI backend from backend/Dockerfile on port 8000, mounts uploads/logs volumes, loads secrets from .env, and gates startup on the database, Redis, and worker being healthy or started.

nodes.name: worker
nodes.summary: Runs the Celery worker (celery -A app.workers.celery_app.celery_app worker) built from the backend image, sharing the uploads/logs volumes and waiting on the database, Redis, and OCR service to be healthy.

nodes.name: ocr
nodes.summary: Builds and runs the PaddleOCR microservice from ocr-service/Dockerfile, exposing port 8080 internally with a health check that the worker's startup gate depends on.

nodes.name: redis
nodes.summary: Runs the official redis:7-alpine image used as the Celery broker/result backend, with a redis-cli ping healthcheck gating dependent services.

nodes.name: db
nodes.summary: Runs the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 Postgres image as the primary datastore for the chatbot database, with a persistent named volume, seeded credentials, a pg_isready healthcheck, and host port 5434 exposed for local access.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Docker build that compiles the Vite/React frontend (npm ci + npm run build) in a node:22-alpine stage, then serves the resulting static bundle from an nginx:alpine runtime image with a wget-based health check on port 80.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build discards the Node.js toolchain in the final image, shipping only the compiled static assets behind nginx to keep the runtime image minimal.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: First build stage (node:22-alpine) that installs npm dependencies via npm ci and runs the production Vite build, producing the /app/dist output consumed by the runner stage.

nodes.name: runner
nodes.summary: Final runtime stage (nginx:alpine) that copies the built frontend assets and nginx.conf into place, exposes port 80, and defines a container healthcheck against the served site.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build for the FastAPI backend: installs Python dependencies from requirements.txt, copies the application source, and on container start runs Alembic migrations before launching Uvicorn to serve app.main:app on port 8000.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-stage build (no multi-stage separation of build/runtime deps) based on python:3.12-slim; the CMD chains `alembic upgrade head` before starting uvicorn so schema migrations run automatically on every container boot.

nodes.name: .dockerignore

nodes.name: 2026-04-20-file-upload-rag-ingestion.md
nodes.summary: Task-by-task implementation plan for the original file upload and RAG ingestion pipeline: a Celery-backed chunk/embed/store flow behind a document upload endpoint, an SSE status endpoint for progress polling, and the docker-compose service topology (frontend, backend, worker, redis, pgvector db) needed to run it, spanning 12 tasks from infrastructure setup through an end-to-end smoke test.
nodes.languageNotes: Structured as a superpowers subagent-driven-development plan: a File Map table followed by numbered tasks with checkbox tracking, intended to be executed task-by-task by an agentic worker rather than read narratively.

nodes.name: 2026-05-05-agentic-rag-chat.md
nodes.summary: Historical implementation plan (superseded 2026-06-28 when the stack moved off self-hosted Ollama to OpenRouter) for the original 'chat with document' feature: a ReAct-style agent that calls a pgvector search tool with a local qwen3 model and streams tokens/citations over SSE, covering the chat endpoint, DocumentSelector UI, and useChat hook across 11 tasks.
nodes.languageNotes: Retains a 'Historical note' banner explaining the plan is kept for context only after the described Ollama/qwen3 stack was replaced by OpenRouter-hosted models.

nodes.name: 2026-05-15-agentic-rag-enhancement.md
nodes.summary: Historical, phased implementation plan (superseded 2026-06-28) for rebuilding the RAG pipeline as a LangGraph CRAG-lite state machine — baseline RAGAS evaluation, parent-child chunking, RRF hybrid retrieval with FlashRank reranking, and a six-node agent graph (rewrite_query, retrieve_and_rerank, grade_chunks, rewrite_and_retry, generate_answer, faithfulness_check) — replacing the original regex-preprocessor and tool-loop agent in `rag.py`.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest of the three plans (2925 lines, 38 sections) organized into five phases (0-4); explicitly supersedes rag.py and directs Phase 4 to update CLAUDE.md and features/chat_with_doc/rag_enhancement.md to reflect the new backend/app/services/rag/ package layout.

nodes.name: 2026-04-20-file-upload-rag-ingestion-design.md
nodes.summary: Approved v1 design spec for file upload and ingestion: a five-service pipeline (React, FastAPI, Redis, Celery worker, PostgreSQL+pgvector) that saves an uploaded PDF/DOCX/image, parses and chunks it, embeds chunks via OpenAI, and notifies the client over SSE when ingestion completes. Documents the original `documents`/`document_chunks` schema, the upload/status API contract, and the specific backend and frontend files the feature touches.
nodes.languageNotes: Early v1 spec — predates OCR support and the later agentic RAG / parent-child chunking enhancements described in the 2026-05-15 spec.

nodes.name: 2026-05-04-agentic-rag-design.md
nodes.summary: Approved-but-superseded design spec for the original 'chat with document' feature: a ReAct agent (qwen3 via Ollama) that iteratively calls a vector-search tool before streaming a grounded answer with citations, plus the DocumentSelector UI, useChat streaming hook, and SSE token/citations/done protocol. Carries a historical note that the stack later moved off Ollama to OpenRouter-hosted models.
nodes.languageNotes: Superseded in part by the 2026-05-15 enhancement spec, which replaces this design's single ReAct tool-loop with a multi-node LangGraph state machine.

nodes.name: 2026-05-15-agentic-rag-enhancement-design.md
nodes.summary: Design spec for the agentic RAG enhancement that replaces the single `rag.py` with the `backend/app/services/rag/` LangGraph package: parent-child chunking, hybrid (vector + FTS) retrieval fused via RRF and reranked with a cross-encoder, and a six-node CRAG-lite state machine (rewrite_query, retrieve_and_rerank, grade_chunks, rewrite_and_retry, generate_answer, faithfulness_check), plus a RAGAS-based evaluation harness and a four-phase rollout plan. This is the architecture CLAUDE.md currently describes as production, with a historical note that the model substrate later moved from Ollama/TEI to OpenRouter.
nodes.languageNotes: Describes a LangGraph StateGraph with conditional edges (grade -> answer | retry | give_up) implementing a Corrective-RAG-lite pattern; also introduces token-based (tiktoken) parent/child chunk sizing in place of character-based splitting.

tour.title: Project Overview: The Real Architecture
tour.description: Start with CLAUDE.md, the project's authoritative guide — not the generic root README, which is leftover create-vite boilerplate and does not describe this project. CLAUDE.md lays out the actual system: a React 19 frontend, a FastAPI backend built around a LangGraph agentic RAG pipeline, hybrid pgvector+Postgres-FTS retrieval reranked via OpenRouter, JWT authentication, Celery background ingestion, and a standalone PaddleOCR microservice. It also documents key conventions (the status='done' field, the eval harness, the reingestion workflow) that recur throughout this tour.

tour.title: Frontend Entry Point
tour.description: The frontend boots the way any Vite app does: index.html loads a module script that executes src/main.jsx, which mounts the root <App/> component inside StrictMode onto the #root div and pulls in the global stylesheet. Everything the user sees — chat UI, login, routing — grows out of this single mount call. From here the tour follows the same path a browser does: down into App.jsx's route table.
tour.languageLesson: React 18+ StrictMode intentionally double-invokes components and effects in development to surface side-effect bugs early; this is expected behavior and does not happen in production builds.

tour.title: Auth State: Context, Token & Repository
tour.description: src/App.jsx wraps the entire route tree in AuthProvider (from AuthContext.jsx), which owns the current user/token/loading state and exposes login/logout plus a useAuth hook to any descendant component. AuthContext delegates HTTP calls to authRepository.js — a repository-pattern module that never calls fetch directly — which in turn goes through the shared client.js API wrapper: that wrapper stores the JWT in localStorage, attaches the Authorization header to every request, and fires a global 'auth:unauthorized' event on any 401 so AuthContext can force a logout. This three-layer split (context -> repository -> client) is the pattern used everywhere the frontend touches the network.
tour.languageLesson: The repository pattern isolates fetch/network calls into dedicated modules (authRepository.js, conversationRepository.js) so React components and hooks never call fetch inline — this keeps components testable and gives you one place to change API behavior.

tour.title: Login Form & Route Guarding
tour.description: LoginPage.jsx is the UI half of the auth flow from Step 3: it collects a username/password, calls the AuthContext login() action, and on success redirects to the page the user originally tried to reach (or /chat by default). That protection is enforced by ProtectedRoute.jsx, a guard component wrapped around the chat route in App.jsx's table — it reads useAuth() and redirects unauthenticated visitors to /login, preserving the intended destination in router state so LoginPage can send them back afterward.

tour.title: Chat UI & the Streaming Hook
tour.description: ChatPage.jsx orchestrates the actual chat experience, wiring together DocumentSelector (choose which ingested document to chat with), ChatThread (the scrollable message list), and the useChat hook. useChat models the conversation as a reducer-based state machine that opens a connection to the backend's SSE-style /api/chat/stream endpoint and parses token, citations, done, and error events as they arrive — this is what makes the assistant's reply appear to type itself in real time. ChatThread renders each turn via ChatMessage, which does lightweight markdown formatting plus an expandable citations panel showing exactly which retrieved chunks backed the answer.
tour.languageLesson: useChat models the conversation with useReducer instead of several useState calls — a reducer centralizes how streaming events (token/citations/done/error) transition state, avoiding the update-ordering bugs that plague ad hoc setState calls during a fast SSE stream.

tour.title: Backend App Factory & Routers
tour.description: backend/app/main.py is the FastAPI counterpart to src/main.jsx — it builds the app, adds request-logging middleware, a health endpoint, and mounts four routers: auth, chat, conversations, and documents. routers/auth.py is the backend side of the login flow from Steps 3-4: it verifies credentials and mints a JWT via security.py, which also exposes the get_current_user OAuth2 dependency that every protected route (including routers/chat.py and routers/documents.py) uses to guard itself. routers/chat.py is the server side of Step 5's useChat hook — it validates the target document, persists conversation/message rows, and streams the agentic RAG answer as server-sent events.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's APIRouter + Depends() pattern lets each router declare its own auth requirement (Depends(get_current_user)) without duplicating token-checking logic — the dependency injection system runs it before the route handler and raises 401 automatically on failure.

tour.title: The Agentic RAG Pipeline: Graph & State
tour.description: When routers/chat.py needs an answer, it calls agentic_rag_stream — the public entry point re-exported from services/rag/__init__.py — which is implemented in graph.py as a LangGraph state machine. graph.py assembles the six-node pipeline previewed in Step 1's CLAUDE.md description, with conditional retry routing, while state.py defines the AgentState TypedDict that flows through every node plus the factory that builds the initial state for a new question. This graph/state split is the backbone the rest of the RAG pipeline builds on.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph models an agent as nodes (functions that transform state) connected by edges — including conditional edges that pick the next node based on state. It's a state machine, not a linear pipeline, which is what allows the retry loop covered in the next step.

tour.title: Six Nodes: Rewrite, Grade, Generate, Verify
tour.description: nodes.py implements the six functions wired together by graph.py: rewrite_query normalizes the user's question, retrieve_and_rerank fetches candidate chunks (Step 9), grade_chunks scores their relevance, rewrite_and_retry loops back with a reformulated query if grading fails, generate_answer produces the response, and faithfulness_check verifies the answer is actually grounded in the retrieved chunks before it's returned. prompts.py holds the prompt templates each of these LLM-calling nodes uses. This CRAG-lite design (corrective RAG with a bounded retry budget) is exactly what the linked design spec describes as the architecture CLAUDE.md now treats as production.

tour.title: Hybrid Retrieval & Reranking
tour.description: retrieval.py is what retrieve_and_rerank (Step 8) actually calls: it runs a pgvector similarity search and a Postgres full-text search in parallel, fuses the two ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), reranks the fused results, applies metadata boosts, and returns parent chunks (~1500 tokens of context) even though the vectors that matched were smaller child chunks (~300 tokens) — a parent/child split that keeps retrieval precise while giving the LLM enough surrounding context. reranker.py is the cross-encoder client behind that rerank step, scoring chunks against the query via OpenRouter's /v1/rerank endpoint and falling back to the original order if the API call fails.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines two independently-ranked lists (vector similarity and keyword/FTS) by summing 1/(k+rank) for each item's position in each list — it needs no score normalization between the two very different scoring systems, which is why it's a common choice for hybrid search.

tour.title: Data Layer: Models, Schemas & Migrations
tour.description: models.py and schemas.py are the two most depended-upon files in the whole backend — nearly every router and service from Steps 6-9 imports one or both. models.py defines the SQLAlchemy ORM tables (documents, parent/child chunks, users, conversations, messages) while schemas.py defines the matching Pydantic request/response shapes that validate API traffic; database.py wires up the engine and the get_db session dependency both layers rely on. The Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/ record how this schema evolved — migration 0004 is the pivotal one, introducing the parent-child chunk tables that Step 9's retrieval logic depends on — while create_users_table.sql is a raw-SQL bootstrap alternative for the users table backing Steps 3-4's JWT auth.
tour.languageLesson: Alembic migrations should be additive and ordered (0001 through 0008 here) so the database schema evolves in lockstep with the ORM models — each file's upgrade()/downgrade() pair makes a schema change reversible.

tour.title: Background Jobs: Ingestion & Celery
tour.description: Before any document can be retrieved (Step 9), it has to be ingested: ingestion.py parses PDFs, DOCX, and images (falling back to OCR for scanned pages), splits the text into the parent/child chunks introduced in Step 10, embeds the child chunks via OpenRouter, and persists everything. That work is too slow to run inside an HTTP request, so routers/documents.py (Step 6) dispatches it to a Celery task defined in workers/tasks.py, configured by celery_app.py (broker/backend wiring plus logging signal handlers) — the task updates the document's status to 'done' or 'failed' with automatic retry on error.
tour.languageLesson: Celery decouples slow work from the request/response cycle: the API enqueues a task and returns immediately, a separate worker process executes it against a broker (Redis here), and the client polls or streams status separately — this is why docker-compose (Step 14) runs 'worker' as its own container distinct from 'backend'.

tour.title: The OCR Microservice
tour.description: When ingestion.py (Step 11) hits a scanned page it can't extract text from directly, it calls ocr_client.py, an HTTP client that ships image bytes to a completely separate service and returns joined text with an averaged confidence score. That service is ocr-service/app.py, a standalone FastAPI app running PaddleOCR/RapidOCR (ONNXRuntime) with its own /ocr endpoint and health check — deployed and scaled independently via its own Dockerfile, which pre-warms the ONNX models at build time so the container starts ready to serve.
tour.languageLesson: Splitting OCR into its own microservice keeps a heavy, compute-intensive ML dependency (ONNXRuntime + PP-OCR models) out of the main backend image, so the backend and the OCR workload can scale and deploy independently.

tour.title: Evaluating the RAG Pipeline
tour.description: Because the RAG pipeline (Steps 7-9) has many tunable knobs — chunk sizes, RRF weights, rerank model choice — the project ships a golden-set evaluation harness. run_eval.py runs every question in golden_set.yaml through agentic_rag_stream, scores the answers with RAGAS-style metrics (faithfulness, relevancy, context precision/recall), and saves timestamped snapshots so two configurations can be compared with --compare. CLAUDE.md instructs running this harness before changing any retrieval or agent code, which is why it carries a dedicated pytest 'eval' marker excluded from normal test runs.

tour.title: Infrastructure & Deployment
tour.description: docker-compose.yml ties every service this tour has covered into one stack: the nginx-served frontend (Step 2's build), the FastAPI backend (Step 6), the Celery worker (Step 11), the PaddleOCR microservice (Step 12), Redis, and a pgvector-enabled Postgres database (Step 10) — wired together with healthchecks and depends_on ordering so, for example, the worker won't start until OCR and the database report healthy. The root Dockerfile multi-stage-builds the frontend (compile in node:22-alpine, serve from nginx:alpine) while backend/Dockerfile runs Alembic migrations before launching Uvicorn; nginx.conf actually serves the built SPA and proxies /api/ to the backend with buffering disabled so Step 5's SSE streaming isn't buffered away.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds (FROM node:22-alpine AS builder ... FROM nginx:alpine) keep build-time tooling (npm, the full node_modules tree) out of the final runtime image — only the compiled dist/ output is copied into the last stage, which is why the production image stays small.
